title: Car broke down on the road: what to do now
h1: Car died or broke down on the road
metaDesc: Your car died or broke down on the road. Hazard lights on, get off the road, and stay buckled inside if it's safe. When to get out and who to call.
first: Turn on your hazard lights and steer as far right, off the road, as you can.
If you're safely off the road, stay inside with your seat belt on and call for help.
If you're stuck in a traffic lane, keep your seat belt on and call 911.

If there's smoke or fire, get everyone out on the side away from traffic, move at least 100 feet from the car and call 911. If you must get out for another reason, wait well away from the car and the road, behind a guardrail if there is one.
Tell the person you call where you are: road name, direction, and the nearest exit or mile marker.
dont: Don't stand between your car and traffic, or right behind your car.
Never try to cross a road with moving traffic.
Don't get out while you're in a traffic lane unless there's smoke or fire.
When the tow truck comes, don't get out or shift to neutral. Wait for the driver to tell you what to do.

steps.t: Ease off the gas, turn on your hazard lights and pull as far right as you can. If the engine died, steering and brakes get much heavier. Hold the wheel firmly and press the brake pedal hard and steady.

Keep your seat belt on and your hazard lights flashing, and call 911. If you have a cloth, hang it out of the window and roll the window up to hold it. Only get out if there's smoke or fire, or help tells you to.

steps.h: If you have to get out
steps.t: Get out on the side away from traffic, usually the passenger side. Walk to a spot behind a guardrail if there is one, well away from the car and the road. If there's smoke or fire, go at least 100 feet away. Take your phone.
Keep your hazard lights on. In snow or bad weather, stay with the car unless it's in danger of being hit. Keep your seat belt on while you wait inside.

call: Call 911 if anyone is hurt, you're stuck in a traffic lane, or you see smoke or fire.
Otherwise call your roadside plan, your insurer's roadside line (on your insurance card or app), or the carmaker's roadside number (in the owner's manual or glovebox).
